title: Deepfake video account opening — virtual bank (demo script)
summary: Synthetic training case. A new customer applies to open an account through video KYC. Two rule signals already show on screen. If the account opens, a large third-party credit arrives within a short time and is split out to an OTC crypto dealer. The trainee must follow the rules first, then decide whether to report or apply enhanced due diligence. This file holds no real customer data and no media files.

rules.note: Two liveness check failures in a row mean the account must not be opened. An override must be recorded as an event. It cannot pass silently.

rules.when: kyc.signals has at least two items, and a sudden third-party credit arrives and is split out
rules.note: Rules come before any model score. This case must not be closed straight away as a false positive.

nodes.title: Video KYC intake
nodes.prompt: The synthetic customer submits an image of an identity document and a video clip. The rules engine has logged an irregular blink rhythm and inconsistent lighting. No decision on opening the account has been made yet.

nodes.title: Accept this video?
nodes.prompt: Both signals are still there. Do you accept the video, ask for a new liveness check, or refuse to open the account?

choices.label: Accept the video and open the account
choices.rationale: This ignores the logged signals. If a sudden burst of funds follows, R2 will require a report or EDD.

choices.label: Ask for a new liveness check
choices.rationale: Get a second observation first, then let R1 decide.

choices.label: Refuse to open the account
choices.rationale: The signals are enough to stop the account opening. There is no need to wait for transactions.

nodes.title: Second liveness check also fails
nodes.prompt: The retry shows the same two signals. Rule R1: after two failures in a row, the account must not be opened.

nodes.title: Override R1?
nodes.prompt: The rule says to refuse the account. You can override it and continue, but the override must stay in the event log.

choices.label: Refuse the account under the rule
Override the rule and open the account
choices.rationale: An allowed teaching branch. The override is itself an event. It does not delete the rule.

nodes.title: Burst of funds after opening
nodes.prompt: Shortly after the account opens, a large third-party credit arrives. It is split at once into two payments and sent to an OTC crypto dealer. Rule R2: when there are deepfake signals and a burst like this, the case must not be closed straight away as a false positive.

nodes.title: How to handle this alert
nodes.prompt: R2 is met. Do you report, apply EDD and freeze, or close it as a false positive?

choices.label: Draft a suspicious transaction report
choices.rationale: The reporting exit that meets R2.

choices.label: Apply EDD and hold outbound payments
choices.rationale: Another exit that meets R2. Stop the account first, then gather more evidence.

choices.label: Close as a false positive
choices.rationale: Poor teaching path. The rule already says the case must not be closed this way.

nodes.title: Account opening refused
nodes.prompt: No account was opened. The signals stay in the twin state. There are no later transactions.

nodes.title: Rule blocks account opening
nodes.prompt: R1 blocked it. The event log should show both liveness check failures, not an oral account given afterwards.

nodes.title: Suspicious transaction report drafted
nodes.prompt: Reporting exit. If R1 was overridden earlier, the override flag stays in the state.

nodes.title: EDD with outbound payments on hold
nodes.prompt: The account is open, but outbound payments are on hold pending EDD.

nodes.title: Closed as a false positive
nodes.prompt: Poor teaching path. R2 was ignored. The dashboard should later mark this session as not following the rules.
